newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK FAIRLY STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK FAIRLY STABLE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted fairly stable against the key U.S. dollar at the close of Friday's quiet interbank trading session, dealers said.

"It was a fairly quiet day today and we were trading within narrower ranges," one dealer commented, saying bid/offer had been kept to a maximum 10 points after widening up to 20 points during the week.

He said the market was likely to see a return to normality next week after the local dollar went on a free fall the past week on the back of import pressure compounded by central bank governor Leonard Tsumba's statements published in a financial newspaper last Friday that the unit was overvalued by five percent against the U.S. dollar.
At Friday's close, the Zimbabwe currency was quoted at 11.5700/6700 on the U.S. dollar from 11.5700/6100 on Thursday but was easier on sterling at 19.0170/0230 compared to 18.9425/19.0195.
It was however a touch firmer at 6.3130/3175 from 6.3190/3390 against the mark but slipped to 2.5290/5325 from 2.5110/5180 against South Africa's rand.
